question: The exploratory analyses of the 400-code sweep and the 126-code Relay Loop page (analyzeRelayLoopOrderEdgeMap11x11.py, analyzeRelayLoopOrderEdgeStory11x11.py) found that two modules of the causal net, switched by the ring's region levels, go with the face: the LOWER CHANNEL (in write, ring bottom -> bg bottom-left or ring left -> bg bottom-left is among the phase's top three transfers) and the FLOOD PUSH (in flood, ring top -> bg top-left is among the top three). Codes with both had a face-like end state (structural overlap >= 0.3) in 45% of cases against 9% for the rest (43% against 6-21% on the 280 space-filling codes alone). Does this hold on NEW codes chosen in advance, by a model frozen before any of them is run, and matched to the controls for how far the ring is from the trained ring?
registeredBefore: the selection of any new code and any new relay run. ALREADY SEEN (so the predictions below are informed by it and it is not tested again): every result for the 400 sweep codes and the 126 Relay Loop page codes, including the module-by-outcome tables, the ring-level windows of the seven near-trained faces and of the two distant ones, and the SVD of the region map. NOT SEEN: the outcome, net or gap of any code in the candidate pool below.
status: CONFIRMATORY; registered before the selection script, the new ring codes and the runs exist.

design.model: Two random forest classifiers (scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier, 200 trees, min_samples_leaf 3, random_state 0) fitted to the 400 sweep codes only, from the ring's four region levels (mean clipped ring value over the cells at folded angles 0-45, 45-90, 90-135 and 135-180 degrees from the top) to (a) the lower channel being present and (b) the flood push being present, each as an edge in the code's per-phase top three of the field-channel net (relayLoopNets.readNet, the page's top-3 view). Frozen: nothing about the new codes is used to refit it.
design.pool: Scrambled Sobol points, seed 20251101, 131072 points over the multipliers [0, 2]^4 of the trained coefficients; keep those whose ring values lie inside [0, 2] G_pol / G_ref with no clipping; drop any whose region levels are within 0.20 (Euclidean, in G_pol / G_ref) of the trained code's region levels.
design.cells: Four cells of 80 codes each, by the frozen model's predicted probabilities (pLower, pPush): BOTH (pLower >= 0.7 and pPush >= 0.7), LOWER ONLY (pLower >= 0.7, pPush <= 0.3), PUSH ONLY (pLower <= 0.3, pPush >= 0.7), NEITHER (both <= 0.3). BOTH is 80 codes drawn at random (numpy default_rng seed 20251102) from its candidates. Each other cell is matched to BOTH one-to-one: for each BOTH code in order of increasing distance from the trained region levels, the unused candidate of the other cell nearest in that distance, accepted if within 0.05. If any cell cannot reach 80, every cell is cut to the size of the smallest (the BOTH codes with the lowest-ranked matches dropped first) and the cut size is reported.
design.runs: Each code through computeBoundaryHarmonicRelay11x11.py (--baseline extraUpdateOnly) and extractRelayLoopSweepRecord11x11.py exactly as the sweep, raw files discarded. Measures per code: observed lower channel and flood push (same definitions), observed reversed lower channel (in write bg bottom-left -> ring bottom, or in clear ring bottom -> mouth, or in flood ring bottom -> bg bottom-left), face overlap at recorded iteration 2173 (boundaryCodeUtilities.structuralIntersectionOverUnion), selectivity gap at the write peak, and the smallest and largest conductance reached.
design.primaryOutcome: face-like end state: structural overlap >= 0.3. Secondary: overlap >= 0.5 (a face), reported as counts only.

V1.criterion: all ring values inside [0, 2] before any run, and the conductance of every cell at every time of every run inside [0, 2] G_ref; any breach voids that code and is reported

V2.criterion: the mean distance from the trained region levels differs by less than 0.03 between any two cells

V3.criterion: no new code is within 0.01 (Euclidean, in multipliers) of any sweep or page code

predictions.name: C1-lowerChannelIsPredictable
predictions.claim: the frozen model predicts the lower channel on unseen codes
predictions.criterion: observed lower-channel presence >= 0.65 among the 160 codes predicted high (BOTH and LOWER ONLY) and <= 0.30 among the 160 predicted low (PUSH ONLY and NEITHER)

predictions.name: C2-floodPushIsPredictable
predictions.claim: the frozen model predicts the flood push on unseen codes
predictions.criterion: observed flood-push presence >= 0.60 among the 160 codes predicted high (BOTH and PUSH ONLY) and <= 0.25 among the 160 predicted low (LOWER ONLY and NEITHER)

predictions.name: C3-bothModulesGoWithTheFace
predictions.claim: the PRIMARY test: with distance from trained matched, the BOTH cell has far more face-like end states than the rest
predictions.criterion: face-like rate in BOTH >= 0.30, exceeding the rate in the other three cells pooled by >= 0.15 (absolute), one-sided Fisher exact p < 0.01

predictions.name: C4-noOtherCellMatchesBoth
predictions.claim: neither module alone does as well
predictions.criterion: the BOTH cell's face-like rate is strictly higher than that of each of LOWER ONLY, PUSH ONLY and NEITHER

predictions.name: C5-theModulesInteract
predictions.claim: the two modules together do more than the sum of their parts
predictions.criterion: difference of differences (BOTH - LOWER ONLY - PUSH ONLY + NEITHER) of face-like rates >= 0.10 and its 95% bootstrap interval (2000 resamples within cells, seed 20251103) excludes 0

predictions.name: C6-gapFollowsTheModules
predictions.claim: the selectivity gap at the write peak follows the modules
predictions.criterion: mean gap in BOTH exceeds the mean of the other three cells' means by >= 0.08

predictions.name: C7-theReversedLowerChannelIsAgainstTheFace
predictions.claim: the mirror-image lower channel works against a face
predictions.criterion: across all new codes, the face-like rate among codes with the reversed lower channel observed is lower than among those without, one-sided Fisher exact p < 0.05

predictions.name: C8-observedModulesNotJustPredicted
predictions.claim: it is the modules actually switched on, not the model's guess, that go with the face
predictions.criterion: across all new codes, the face-like rate among those with BOTH modules observed is >= 0.30 and exceeds that among the rest by >= 0.15, one-sided Fisher exact p < 0.01

predictions.name: C9-neitherCellIsQuiet
predictions.claim: without either module a face-like end state is rare

reporting: Every criterion is reported verbatim with its number, including those that fail or reverse. If C3 fails, the exploratory association is not confirmed as a property of the modules (it may have been proximity to the trained ring or chance across many looks) and the module story is withdrawn as an explanation. Anything computed afterwards beyond these is labelled exploratory.
